standard.title: Jute Agrotextiles for Growth of Plants and Suppression of Weeds — Specification
standard.sector: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agro-tech
ics_code: Not specified in the provided source text

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agro-tech Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements of nonwoven jute agrotextiles (JAT) used for the growth of plants and the suppression of weeds. The selection of the specific jute agrotextile is decided principally based on the topography of the site, gradient of the slope, annual rainfall, nature of the soil, and the type of weeds and plants.

certification.description: Voluntary Certification Scheme (ISI Mark Scheme). Conforming products may be certified as per the conformity assessment schemes of the Bureau of Indian Standards in accordance with the BIS Act, 2016, and carry the Standard Mark. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to agricultural jute fabrics.
requirements: The nonwoven jute agrotextiles must meet all specified physical, chemical, and mechanical requirements given in Table 1.
Lot sampling for conformance inspection must be drawn strictly in accordance with IS 14706.

Packing of JAT rolls must conform to IS 4744. The standard explicitly warns that prolonged storage of packed material or its exposure to the open must be avoided to prevent premature environmental degradation.

Unless otherwise agreed, each roll must be stenciled with an indelible ink of a suitable colour with: a) Product identification; b) Length and width in metres; c) Type of material (Type 1, Type 2, or Type 3); d) Roll Number/Lot number; and e) Other declarations required by the law in force.

Puncture resistance is evaluated using a tensile testing machine (Annex B). A test specimen is clamped without tension between circular plates of a ring clamp attachment. A solid steel rod attached to the load indicator exerts force against the centre of the unsupported portion until physical rupture occurs. Puncture resistance is recorded as the maximum force achieved.
The average puncture resistance must be calculated from 5 tested specimens, alongside the standard deviation read directly from the recording instrument.
Prior to JAT installation for planting, the ground surface must be dressed, cleared of all foreign materials, and prepared to the required level.

Two fabric pieces with proper '+' cut marks must be laid side by side keeping zero gaps between them. The plant is planted directly on the '+' cut mark. The four corners of the cut portion must be tucked/inserted inside the cloth to keep the surroundings of the plant's girth free.
The desired plants (such as vegetables, fruits, or similar) must be planted onto the exposed ground, maintaining a safe distance between individual plants.
Watering may be conducted occasionally, specifically in cases of an extremely dry climate.
